extracted.subtask_description: Organizational editorial and ethical standards for Reuters journalists and newsroom staff, covering accuracy, sourcing, independence, visual standards, conflicts of interest, use of AI, and conduct inside and outside work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the Trust Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the Trust Principles in all activities related to Reuters News.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Trust Principles underpin independence and impartiality; staff should raise potential conflicts with managers and consult Ethics and Standards where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold accuracy sacrosanct
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy is at the heart of what we do: get it first but above all get it right; accuracy and balance take precedence over speed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before publishing, consider how to withstand challenge or denial; accuracy applies to facts, datelines, bylines, captions, scripts and images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek fair comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek fair comment — give subjects an opportunity to respond and ensure reporting allows readers to understand differing views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations should not be portrayed as fact; charges should not be conveyed as a sign of guilt; where possible, talk to sources on all sides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct errors transparently
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters is transparent about errors and rectifies them promptly, clearly and comprehensively whether in a story, caption, graphic or script.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections should be visible and comprehensive; handle complaints promptly and escalate when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strive for balance and freedom from bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Strive for balance and freedom from bias — be scrupulously fair and balanced and avoid taking sides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let nationality or politics influence coverage; choose words carefully to avoid implying bias; give subjects opportunity to put their side.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose potential or actual conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose potential or actual conflicts of interest to a manager.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there's a perceived conflict (e.g., personal investment, family links, outside activities), raise it with your manager; Reuters may reassign duties if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid injecting unattributed opinion in a news story
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not inject unattributed opinion into news stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opinion belongs only in clearly labeled opinion pieces; journalists must not express personal views in news files, voiced video, scripts, blogs or chat rooms they contribute to in their work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not fabricate or plagiarise
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not fabricate facts or plagiarise material; be honest about origins of material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failing to attribute or misrepresenting origins (e.g., labelling 'handout' without source) risks charges of plagiarism and reputational damage and may lead to disciplinary measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not alter still images or video beyond normal editorial preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not alter still images or video footage beyond the methods normally used to prepare content for editorial use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visual journalism must reflect unaltered reality; actions that add to or detract from reality may be fabrication and can cause serious reputational damage; decisions on graphic material usually require senior editor approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not pay for information or accept bribes or trade on privileged information
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not pay for information or accept a bribe or trade on privileged information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Never take or offer payment for a story; facilitation payments not permitted; accepting gifts above nominal value should be declined or surrendered to manager; travel/accommodation offers require manager approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy requires honesty in sourcing, cross-checking information and taking care with dates, bylines and datelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use named sources where possible; verify unnamed sources' track record/motive; record interviews when allowed; cross-check wherever possible; accuracy may justify delaying publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections (process)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rectify errors promptly, clearly and comprehensively in all formats (story, caption, graphic, script).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complaints should be investigated promptly; acknowledge and follow up complaints that cannot be immediately resolved; handle at senior level and escalate to Ethics and Standards when in doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sourcing (named vs unnamed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer named sources; use unnamed sources only when necessary and when they provide information of market or public interest not available on the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Press sources to go on record; single-source anonymous stories are exceptional and require special authorization; be explicit about what you do not know; protecting source confidentiality may require disclosure to supervisors on legitimate editorial grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sourcing (verification and cross-check)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-check information, seek two or more sources where possible, and weigh unnamed sources' credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess an unnamed source’s track record, position and motive; try to disprove as well as prove when doing initiative reporting; be cautious about imposters and about communications that can be interfered with.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotes are sacrosanct: never alter except to delete redundant words or clauses without changing sense; give context and body language that affects meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid cleaning up turns of phrase to make someone look better or exposing them to ridicule; consider paraphrase or consult a senior journalist when in doubt; translations should be idiomatic and preserve tone; correct minor grammatical errors only where valid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflecting reality (avoid sensationalism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Images and stories must reflect reality and avoid hype or sensationalism that misleads readers/viewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider word choice (e.g., 'flood' vs small numbers); visual actions that alter reality may constitute fabrication; consider market/customer sensitivities across platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Datelines and bylines
rubrics_metrics.description: Bylines should show the writer was at the dateline; only use datelines where Reuters staff/freelancers were present on the spot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributors should be credited in an additional-reporting line with name and location; do not byline from locations where staff were not present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Properly attribute material that is not ours, including photos and video, so customers can assess reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label the source clearly (e.g., 'Greenpeace Video' or 'U.S. Army Photo'); simply saying 'handout' is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting rumours
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim to report facts rather than rumours; when rumours affect markets, try to verify or knock them down.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptional circumstances may justify moving a story before verification when markets are moving violently; still, differentiate fact from rumour and explain context to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic images and obscenities
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not publish graphic images, obscene language or gratuitous details without a valid news reason; consider distress and dignity of subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Senior editor decision usually required; consider necessity to understanding; warn audiences (e.g., 'Warning: Graphic Content' before packaged videos); be mindful of different market thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain independence and avoid conflicts of interest or situations that create perceptions of bias; editors and staff must not let commercial interests influence coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss potential conflicts with managers; Trust Principles and Founders Share Company Board protect editorial independence; examine complaints about balance impartially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal investments
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not let personal or immediate family investments influence your reporting or editing; avoid trading or reporting on entities in which you have interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not trade in securities where you have material non-public information; follow Thomson Reuters Code of Conduct on investments; breaches may lead to discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaring financial interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure no circumstances create suspicion of bias due to financial interests; follow company Code of Conduct requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose interests and seek guidance; failure to adhere to Code of Conduct may result in disciplinary procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work outside Reuters
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not engage in paid outside work without manager permission; permission routinely granted if activities don't affect Reuters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes writing books, speaking, commercial photography; NewsGuild members in US have limited exceptions; check for competition or conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checking back with sources (vetting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not submit stories to sources for vetting before publication; checking back may be done to verify quotes but must not allow sources to retract or alter quotes to their advantage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist requests to approve quotes; if quotes are submitted for approval, do not agree to material changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gifts and entertainment
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not accept payments, gifts or benefits from news sources that could create obligations or perceptions of bias; nominal traditional gifts may be acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use value as test: nominal gifts may be accepted; gifts of more than nominal value should be declined or surrendered to manager; avoid 'junkets' and excessive hospitality; ask manager when in doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel and accommodation from sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters pays its own way; accept free travel/accommodation only with managerial permission and when story warrants coverage or access otherwise impossible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptional circumstances (war zones, remote famine) may justify acceptance with reimbursement efforts; managers normally require permission; avoid offers that could create perceived obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bribes and other inducements
rubrics_metrics.description: Never take or offer payment (cash or in kind) for a news story; bribery is a grave breach and grounds for dismissal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply with anti-bribery policy; be aware of local laws restricting officials from accepting benefits; seek approval before offering any gift; facilitation payments prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence within Reuters (editorial vs commercial)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not alter coverage to help clinch business deals or suit commercial interests; preserve editorial independence from the commercial side of Thomson Reuters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If non-editorial colleagues raise concerns, examine them for reasoned arguments but resist commercial influence; editorial duty is to accuracy, balance and truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entering competitions and receiving awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees may submit Reuters work for reputable journalism awards with manager approval and only to contests judged by journalists; avoid contests with self-serving sponsors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions must have managerial approval; work should not be produced primarily for awards or altered except to conform to contest rules; approval process for non-journalist-judged contests involves senior editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity (personal conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to highest ethical standards and the Trust Principles, acting with personal integrity at all times and respecting local laws and cultures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid conduct that could confuse personal views with Reuters; treat colleagues and sources with dignity and respect; report perceived breaches without fear of recrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying ourselves as journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should not obtain news by deception or pretend to be other than journalists; identify as Reuters journalists if directly questioned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In some circumstances allowing an assumption to persist may be acceptable in interests of newsgathering—apply common sense and consult Code of Conduct and manager when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting from the Internet
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the same standards of sourcing, identification and verification to online reporting as in other newsgathering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take precautions online similar to offline; do not use material that is not sourced and verifiable; verify provenance of online material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insider trading
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff must not buy or sell securities while in possession of material non-public information, nor tip others; such conduct is forbidden and may be criminal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material information examples are provided (mergers, forecasts, earnings, etc.); treat information obtained at work as non-public until widely disclosed and market has absorbed it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with sources (professional conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cultivate sources professionally, be polite and fair, maintain detachment and avoid close relationships that could raise questions about bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid spending excessive leisure time with a source; disclose romantic or family attachments to management; do not report on or quote family members to avoid perceptions of favouritism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with customers (editorial/commercial separation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain professional boundaries with customers who may also be news sources; avoid negotiating sales contracts or commercial activity as journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussions should be limited to news issues and product functionality; guard the separation between editorial and commercial functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with people (sensitivity and accuracy)
rubrics_metrics.description: When covering people in the news, treat victims sensitively, avoid needless pain and offence, seek clear accounts, avoid sensationalism and be alert to spin and bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists should show integrity, impartiality, persistence, accountability and humility; be able to defend stories to sources and readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with competitors
rubrics_metrics.description: Compete vigorously but avoid improper or illegal means of collecting information; acknowledge competitors' exclusives and attribute accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not make informal deals, trade material or divulge editorial policies; cooperation allowed when it reduces risk to life or is in mutual interest (e.g., staff safety, restricted access).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate complaints promptly, acknowledge them when immediate investigation isn't possible, and handle them at an appropriate senior level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain constructive attitude; escalate to Ethics and Standards when in doubt; prompt, proper responses can avoid legal problems and bad publicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with the authorities (requests for material)
rubrics_metrics.description: Refer any requests for published or unpublished Reuters content or journalists' materials from authorities to a senior editor and the editorial legal team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not voluntarily hand over unpublished material; consider legal challenges to subpoenas where appropriate to protect staff safety and independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dealing with each other (workplace conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Teamwork and cooperation across disciplines is required; staff must be able to raise concerns about standards and ethics without fear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foster an environment free from harassment; share non-confidential information and ideas; treat colleagues with dignity and respect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting incidents (internal process)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report serious incidents (harm to staff, hoaxes, improper behaviour, etc.) to supervisors so senior officials can take corrective action and spot trends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-managerial staff must report incidents to supervisors; swift reporting helps manage reputational risk and operational safety globally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Life outside Reuters (private conduct impacts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure personal activities do not create confusion between professional activities and private opinions; be cautious using company systems for personal views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid political or investment commentary on Reuters systems that could identify Reuters with a cause; use private addresses when in doubt and consult manager.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom from bias (neutrality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Park nationality and politics at the door; maintain neutrality to enable reporting on all sides of issues without agenda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive to be scrupulously fair; be careful with language that implies siding; give appropriate space to parties according to news judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take no side, tell all sides
rubrics_metrics.description: Never identify with any side in an issue, conflict or dispute; reflect all sides in text and visual stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objectivity doesn't always mean equal space; news judgment dictates appropriate emphasis; always ask 'What do I know?' and 'What do I need to know?'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opinion and Analysis (clear labeling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly distinguish fact-based news from labeled opinion pieces; journalists must not express personal opinions in news reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opinion pieces must be labeled and disclaimers used; columnists should express grounded views in their expertise and avoid ungrounded provocation or personal attacks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discriminatory language and stereotypes
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid inappropriate references to gender, ethnicity, religion, culture, appearance, age and sexual orientation and be sensitive to unconscious stereotyping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use neutral language; avoid gratuitous references to appearance; prefer neutral role descriptors (e.g., executives, journalists) over gender-specific tags; be cautious with country stereotypes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not express personal views on investments; value judgments on investments must be sourced to a named third party and Reuters does not give investment advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local laws may prohibit giving investment advice; journalists should not give investment advice to readers or customers by any means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting on Thomson Reuters (extra safeguards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise extreme care when reporting on Thomson Reuters or affiliates to avoid bias; stories must be seen before publication by senior editors and include company comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories should include comment from a company spokesman and be cleared with Managing/Regional Editor and Global Editor for Ethics and Standards; only pick up stories likely to be market-moving or of significant general interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political and Community Activity (outside work)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters staff must not give support to any political party or group or identify Reuters with any side; outside political displays may raise perceptions of bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff retain rights to vote and participate in civic life but must consider how activities might be perceived; consult managers when in doubt; perceptions of conflicts may require reassignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal Opportunity in the Newsroom
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat employees fairly regardless of gender, ethnicity, national or religious background, age, disability, marital/parental status or sexual orientation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection for jobs, training and promotion should be determined by skills and abilities and follow applicable laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity in the Newsroom
rubrics_metrics.description: Embrace diversity of thought, style, experience, culture, race, gender identity and other characteristics to enrich journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diversity brings perspectives that improve coverage and debate about the news; welcome varying viewpoints in newsroom practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media Interviews and Speaking Engagements
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews and speaking engagements must be approved in advance by the journalist’s manager and the communications team and must adhere to editorial standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews should come from credible outlets; correspondents must not give personal opinions; payment should not be sought or accepted; priority to Reuters' own services; seek approval before participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conferences (participation rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Attendance or speaking at conferences requires editorial approval and must not undermine Reuters' integrity; limits apply on moderation and participation when sponsors pay panelists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists should moderate only if Reuters controls content; avoid panels with paid panelists or product-launch aims; editors limited to one company event per year; no payment for participation; seek communications approval before speaking to outside media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artificial Intelligence and Generative AI
rubrics_metrics.description: Use AI tools cautiously: maintain editorial accountability, be transparent about GenAI use, never use generative AI to create or enhance imagery, and verify all AI-generated facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI may assist non-visual tasks (shotlists, captions) only with approval; do not upload Reuters/partner content to non-approved external tools; never trust unverified AI-generated facts — independently verify and fact-check; seek guidance from Ethics and Standards or Legal when in doubt.
